A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WUSH research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 3 reports original quantization losses and Llama/Qwen benchmark accuracy in Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–4.

after.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendix B report original quantization losses, model accuracy, C4 KL-divergence results and GPU measurements.

M1.justification: The closed-form WUSH construction is retained, but v2 Algorithm 1 adds GPTQ integration with interleaved transform construction and intra-block/inter-block error propagation, alongside an RTN fallback. This implements a substantive procedure that v1 explicitly left as future work.

E1.justification: V2 adds C4 evaluation following FineWeb calibration (Appendix B, Table 3). The existing FineWeb-Edu layer-loss evaluation and LM Evaluation Harness/Platinum task coverage are retained. Additional model sizes expand configurations rather than dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: V1's end-to-end comparisons primarily use identity and Hadamard transforms with RTN. V2 Table 2 adds reported comparisons with SmoothQuant, QuaRot, SpinQuant, GPTQ-I and GPTQ-H/MR-GPTQ. GPTQ comparators also enter retained Platinum experiments, while Figure 2 introduces GPU comparisons against QuTLASS Hadamard-plus-quantization and bare FP4 kernels.

E3.justification: V2 introduces GPTQ evaluation, Qwen3-32B accuracy experiments, C4 KL-divergence measurement and BF16-normalized GPU throughput tests. The latter specify RTX 5090, batch size 1024, group size 32 and multiple layer shapes, including Llama-3.1-70B. The original layer-loss protocol remains 32 calibration samples of length 2048.

E4.justification: The original WUS-removal and layer-loss ablation is retained. V2 Section 5 and Figure 2 add an overhead analysis comparing bare FP4 GEMM, Hadamard-plus-quantization and WUSH-plus-quantization, examining the runtime cost of using distinct adaptive transforms across blocks.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly states that results are aggregated over multiple random seeds, including the C4 results. V1 already reports ten-run random-rotation averages and Platinum standard deviations. V2 does not establish increased run counts or introduce significance tests, and exact seed counts remain unspecified.

E6.justification: V2 adds GPTQ, C4, Qwen3-32B and GPU results and revises existing entries. Qwen3-8B MXFP4 RTN-WUSH average accuracy changes from 75.45 in v1 Table 2 to 74.91 in v2 Table 4. Llama-3.1-8B MXFP4 RTN-WUSH remains 73.21 while RTN-H changes from 71.47 to 70.45. These are reported-result revisions; complete cross-version protocol equivalence is not documented. Table 1 changes only scaling and rounding.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix A.1 adds a decomposition-invariance lemma and proof, and Appendix A.3 supplies derivations for previously asserted special cases. The central optimality theorem, quantization-noise models and Gaussian/Laplacian bounds are retained; much of the expanded appendix relocates existing mathematics.

C1.justification: V2 extends the claimed contributions from closed-form transforms with preliminary RTN evidence to GPTQ integration and efficient GPU implementation. Its abstract and introduction claim quantified W4A4 advantages and up to 6.6-fold per-layer throughput. The abstract and conclusion also qualify the earlier blanket optimality wording to near-optimality.

C2.justification: V2 Appendix A.2 explains why equalizing coordinate marginals can leave multivariate outliers intact. Section 6 adds explanations involving NVFP4's group size and top-element preservation, and qualifies NVFP4 accuracy gains as often within run-to-run variability. The earlier interpretation of MXFP4 as exhibiting mixed FP/INT behavior remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds detailed GPTQ pseudocode, CUTLASS kernel design, transform storage layout, tiling and hardware information, plus a source-code link. Appendix B newly discloses emulated BF16/FP16 quantization, disabled Qwen thinking mode and the Llama MMLU-CoT reporting convention. These disclosures do not establish that those existing evaluation settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 positions MR-GPTQ as the state-of-the-art comparison target, discusses its QuTLASS kernels and connects the integration to Chen et al.'s GPTQ formulation. The underlying cited works are retained; changes such as FlatQuant's publication update are bibliographic rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 separates Related Work and Methodology from the introduction, moves the algorithm before the theory, and relocates extensive derivations into Appendix A. It substantially rewrites the abstract and explanatory narrative, introduces dedicated GPU coverage and reorganizes the experimental presentation.

P2.justification: V2 adds geometric and approximation illustrations, GPU speedup plots and a KL-divergence table. Accuracy tables are restructured, while existing Platinum heatmaps and boxplots are enlarged, arranged vertically and largely moved to Appendix B. Table 1 changes its displayed scale to 10^-3.

improvement.justification: V1 left GPTQ integration and efficient kernels as open problems; v2 supplies an algorithm, implementation details and measured evidence addressing both. Broader baseline comparisons and reproducibility disclosures substantially strengthen practical validation. A material caveat is that the headline 6.6-fold speedup corresponds to bare FP4 in Figure 2; WUSH including transformation and quantization peaks near 5.8-fold. This overstatement and incomplete seed details temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains.
